1492 is remembered for Columbus. On the map of Europe the same year also closed Muslim rule in Iberia and expelled Jews from Spain.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ On 2 January 1492 Boabdil surrendered Granada to Castile and Aragon. It ended the last Islamic rule on the Iberian Peninsula after a war that ran from 1482. The marriage of Isabella and Ferdinand in 1469 had joined their crowns.
2/ On 31 March 1492 the Alhambra Decree ordered unconverted Jews out of Castile and Aragon by 31 July. Estimates of those expelled range from about 40,000 to 100,000.
3/ Many Sephardic Jews went to Portugal, but only gained a few years of safety before forced conversion. Ottoman sultan Bayezid II sent ships to bring others to cities like Thessaloniki and Izmir.
4/ Spain formally revoked the decree on 16 December 1968. In 2015 it passed a dual-citizenship law for descendants, which expired in 2019.

5/ Columbus left Palos on 3 August 1492 with three ships and sighted land on the night of 11 October. He believed he had reached islands off Asia. The Caribbean's 'West Indies' name comes from that error.
6/ Meanwhile in the north, Denmark, Norway and Sweden were still joined in the Kalmar Union, founded in 1397. Sweden left for good in 1523, when Gustav Vasa was elected king.
One year, three very different turning points. Which one do you think mattered most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
